guide_enrichment.narrative: We are not reacting simply to the opening-week scores. For us, the more relevant connection is that Syracuse produced 238 rushing yards while California allowed 277 on the ground. Results against different opponents do not transfer automatically, but that combination gives Syracuse a plausible way to control the game without relying entirely on its passing efficiency.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We will be watching Syracuse’s passing offense against California’s pass defense. Our underlying numbers identify this as California’s clearest advantage, making it the primary concern for our position. Steve Angeli threw for 263 yards in his return, and Syracuse’s offensive line received an 87.0 PFF pass-blocking grade in the opener, but one performance against New Hampshire does not settle this matchup. If Syracuse keeps Angeli comfortable enough to complement the running game, we think the broader paths supporting our wager remain intact.

recent_game.fact: Syracuse opened the season with a 66-3 home win over New Hampshire.
Syracuse scored 41 first-half points, produced 238 rushing yards and finished with 513 total yards against New Hampshire.
The Orange held New Hampshire to three points and 159 total yards while recording five sacks and nine tackles for loss.
Syracuse gained three turnovers and committed no turnovers in the opener.
Syracuse was penalized 12 times for 125 yards against New Hampshire.

opponent_notes.fact: California opened the season with a 45-24 home loss to UCLA.
Cal allowed 277 rushing yards and 184 passing yards against UCLA.
Cal running back A. Mohammed carried 28 times for 120 yards and one touchdown in the opener.
Cal totaled 410 yards and held the ball for 34:49 in its opener.
Cal receivers I. Strong, C. Hendricks and M. Mason combined for 15 catches, 218 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1.

quarterback.fact: Syracuse starting quarterback Steve Angeli returned from his 2025 season-ending injury and passed for 263 yards against New Hampshire.
Angeli has passed for at least 230 yards in six consecutive games and has never thrown for fewer than 245 yards in a Syracuse appearance.
Angeli has completed 176 of 265 career passes for 2,352 yards, 23 touchdowns and three interceptions across Syracuse and Notre Dame.
Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed 24 of 41 passes for 271 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions against UCLA.
Sagapolutele led the ACC with 24.31 completions per game as a freshman in 2025.
Syracuse's projected quarterback depth chart lists Angeli first, followed by Amari Odom or Malachi Nelson.

offensive_personnel.fact: True freshman running back Shavane Anderson Jr. rushed 10 times for 102 yards and three touchdowns in his collegiate debut.
Running back Tylik Hill made his first career start and rushed 16 times for 91 yards and his first collegiate touchdown.
Transfer running backs Ahmad Miller and Ju'Juan Johnson did not play against New Hampshire but are expected to make their Syracuse debuts against Cal.
Miller transferred from Jackson State after leading the SWAC with 1,054 rushing yards and nine touchdowns in 2025.
Wide receiver Umari Hatcher caught eight passes for career highs of 147 yards and two touchdowns in the opener after missing the 2025 season due to injury.
Tight end David Clement set career highs with two catches for 35 yards and scored his first collegiate touchdown on a 27-yard reception.
Syracuse's projected starting offensive line is Trevion Mack at left tackle, Oluwafunto Akinshilo at left guard, Joe Cruz at center, Byron Washington at right guard and Kam Pringle at right tackle.
The Syracuse offensive line received an 87.0 PFF pass-blocking grade in Week 1, second best among ACC teams through Saturday's games.
Center Joe Cruz has appeared in 38 games with 17 starts and has allowed one sack in 657 pass-blocking opportunities, according to PFF.
Akinshilo, a 2026 transfer, made his first career start at guard against New Hampshire.

defensive_personnel.fact: Four of Syracuse's five sacks against New Hampshire were recorded by transfers.
Transfer edge defender Keyshawn Johnson recorded 2.5 sacks, four tackles and a forced fumble in his Syracuse debut.
Johnson transferred from UT Martin after setting its program record with 13.5 sacks in 2025.
Transfer defensive lineman Tunmise Adeleye tied his career high with six tackles and recorded a sack in his Syracuse debut.
Defensive lineman Rashard Perry, whose 2025 season ended with an injury after five games, recorded three tackles and his first career interception in the 2026 opener.
Cornerback Chris Peal allowed 14 receiving yards when targeted and led Syracuse with four solo tackles against New Hampshire, according to PFF.
Syracuse's projected defensive front lists Tunmise Adeleye and Keyshawn Johnson at end with Nissi Ogbebor and Rashard Perry at defensive tackle.

coaching_changes.fact: Vince Kehres is in his first season as Syracuse's defensive coordinator.
Alex Bayer is in his first season as Syracuse's special-teams coordinator.
Cal head coach Tosh Lupoi is in his first season and will coach his first road game as a head coach at Syracuse.

Cal's offensive coordinator Jordan Somerville, co-offensive coordinator Ike Hilliard, defensive coordinator Michael Hutchings and co-defensive coordinator Da'Von Brown are all in their first seasons with the program.
Jeff Nixon is Syracuse's offensive coordinator and operates from the booth.

injury_availability.fact: Steve Angeli played in the opener after suffering a season-ending injury against Clemson in Week 4 of the 2025 season.
Ahmad Miller and Ju'Juan Johnson are expected to play against Cal after not appearing in the opener.
Freshman wide receiver Calvin Russell III is expected to return to the field in October.
Umari Hatcher returned in the opener after missing the 2025 season due to injury.

offensive_context.fact: Ten Syracuse players recorded a reception against New Hampshire.
Five different Syracuse players scored a rushing or receiving touchdown in the opener.
Syracuse converted 66.7 percent of its third downs in Week 1.

In 18 consecutive games with offensive coordinator Jeff Nixon's Week 1 starting quarterback available, Syracuse quarterbacks have passed for at least 250 yards; the Orange are 14-4 and average 471.4 yards and 36.8 points during that span.

defensive_context.fact: Syracuse allowed 60 rushing yards and 99 passing yards in the opener.
Twenty-four Syracuse defenders recorded at least one tackle against New Hampshire, and nine players had at least half a tackle for loss.
Syracuse did not allow a touchdown or a red-zone score in Week 1.

special_teams.fact: Davien Kerr blocked a punt that went out of the end zone for a safety against New Hampshire.
Demetres Samuel Jr. returned four punts for 83 yards, including a 38-yard return, and added a 42-yard safety-kick return in the opener.
Kerr also returned two punts for 50 yards against New Hampshire.
Kicker Tripp Woody made a 34-yard field goal in the opener and is 11-for-11 in his career on attempts inside 40 yards.
Freshman Jimmy Gregg is listed as Syracuse's projected starting punter after punting twice in his collegiate debut.

series_context.fact: Syracuse leads the all-time series with California 2-1 and won the most recent meeting 33-25 at Cal in 2024.
This is Cal's first game in the JMA Wireless Dome and its first trip to Syracuse since 1967.
In the 2024 meeting, Syracuse scored on its first six drives and made four field goals.

other_relevant.fact: The game is Syracuse's 2026 ACC opener; the Orange have won three of their last four conference openers.
Five Syracuse players made their first FBS starts against New Hampshire, including first career starts for Tylik Hill, Jimmy Gregg and Nissi Ogbebor.
Syracuse used 84 players in the opener, including 45 freshmen or sophomores.
